mutations.name: new does not force saving, so it prints the plan and writes nothing
mutations.comment: The whole documented function of `new`. An exit-code assertion cannot catch it: `schema plan` with no save destination prints the document and exits 0, so only asserting the FILE separates the two.

mutations.name: new behaves like --dry-run instead of writing the plan file
new registers --save defaulted to true instead of forcing it
mutations.old: flags.BoolVar(&opts.edit, "edit", false, "Edit the plan in the terminal editor")
mutations.new:
flags.BoolVar(&opts.edit, "edit", false, "Edit the plan in the terminal editor")
	flags.BoolVar(&opts.save, "save", true, "Save the plan to a local plan file")
mutations.comment: The plausible alternative implementation. It writes the file on a bare invocation and therefore passes the behavior tests, but it accepts `--save=false` — a flag Atlas does not register on this sub-verb — and quietly turns the verb into a no-op.

mutations.comment: stdout must stay machine-readable; the note exists precisely because it can be ignored by a pipeline reading stdout.

mutations.name: new reports the parent verb in its diagnostics
mutations.comment: A refusal naming `atlas schema plan` after the operator typed `atlas schema plan new` sends them to a different command's help and a different flag set.

mutations.name: new accepts positional arguments
mutations.comment: The captured Atlas usage line is `atlas schema plan new [flags]`; the parent's is `atlas schema plan [flags] [name]`.

mutations.name: new allows --name and --name-format together
validate skips the from-fingerprint gate
mutations.comment: Killed only by the idempotent-plan fixture: with an ordinary drifted target the replay fails too, so this mutation would survive on every other input in the suite.

mutations.name: the from-fingerprint gate keys on the fingerprint shape alone
mutations.comment: The `sha256:` shape is public. A JSON plan whose from_fingerprint is simply not in that form must not be able to switch the gate off.

mutations.name: validate reuses the apply rehearsal policy and skips the replay
mutations.comment: Under the apply policy a fingerprint-verified native plan with no --dev-url is not replayed at all, so validate would report a plan valid against a desired state it cannot reach.

mutations.name: validate applies the plan to the target after verifying it
mutations.comment: The protected state, not the proxy: this mutation still exits 0 and still prints nothing, and is caught only by re-introspecting the target.

mutations.name: validate reports success on stdout
validate accepts --exclude and verifies a different transition
the missing --to wording also swallows a missing --from
mutations.comment: This is the blanket-rule shape that cost a predecessor a whole migration history: a substitution keyed on a symptom rather than on the specific error swallows every other diagnostic that shares the symptom. `errors.Is(err, err)` is always true for the non-nil err reaching this branch and exists only to keep the errors import in use; dropping it is a build failure, which is not a result.

mutations.name: validate treats --file as optional
validate accepts a registry plan URL
validate accepts positional arguments
the sub-verbs stop refusing what the parent refuses
the shared transition registration drops a flag Atlas registers
mutations.old: flags.String("lock-timeout", "", "Timeout for acquiring the database lock")
mutations.comment: Drift away from the captured Atlas flag set. Caught by the surface pin, not by any behavior test — the flag is refused anyway, so nothing else notices it disappearing.

mutations.name: --from may be a schema file rather than the target database
the parent verb name is lost, so every shared diagnostic goes unnamed
the transition config resolution is skipped, so --env stops feeding the plan
mutations.comment: The extraction of this block out of runAtlasSchemaPlan is a refactor; this proves the moved code is still reached from the parent verb.

mutations.name: validate stops guarding --dev-url against the target database
mutations.comment: MEASURED consequence, not a hypothetical: with this field dropped, `validate --dev-url <target>` resets the target destructively and applies the plan, then exits 0 with empty stdout. On a target holding keep_me with 3 rows: before = tables [keep_me], 3 rows; after = tables [added, keep_me], 0 rows. The entire suite stayed green before the guard subtest existed, which is why it is pinned by state (tables AND row count), not by the message.

mutations.name: validate ignores the exclude patterns the plan records
mutations.comment: The inverse of this PR's invariant: validate then refuses a plan `schema apply --plan` accepts, because the comparison sees an object the plan was explicitly computed without. Killed only by a fixture whose plan carries --exclude patterns; every other fixture here is computed without them and so cannot tell the two apart.

mutations.name: the validate provenance note names the parent verb
mutations.comment: The note is the whole provenance contract; naming the wrong command sends the operator to a different verb's flag set. The `new` side already pins this.
